name: Euler Finance: copied exploit contract executes the DAI-market exploit first, proceeds routed to the hacker by a hard-coded destination
verdict_reason: Sub-type: copy-of-contract front-run that captured nothing (the copier's own contract paid the hacker). (1) Real attacker = EOA 0xB2698C2D99aD2C302a95A8Db26B08d17A77CEdd4 (funded by Tornado Cash 1 ETH pool) which deployed exploit contract 0x036cec1a... in block 16817993 idx 35 (tx 0x50dc9c91..., 3 gwei tip). (2) One block later (16817994 idx 5, tx 0x725db76c...) a different EOA 0x5F259D0b... deployed a contract whose creation calldata is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the attacker's (17,115 bytes) except 4 occurrences of the 20-byte address 0xB2698C2D... replaced by 0x5F259D0b... (80 differing bytes; incidents/euler-copybot-2023/bytecode_diff.json); the hard-coded 0xb66cd966... (profit/withdraw destination) was left untouched. (3) In block 16817996 idx 0 (tx 0xc310a0af..., 37.9 gwei tip, top of block by gas price) the copier called the DAI-market entry point (0x863df8af) of its copy: Aave flash loan 30M DAI -> Euler exploit -> 38,904,507.35 DAI out of Euler, 30,027,000 DAI repaid, 8,877,507.35 DAI net left in the copy. The hacker never called that entry point on its own contract; its own first attack call (WETH market, tx 0xa476fad7, block 16818013 idx 44) came 17 blocks (~3.5 min) later and failed out-of-gas, first success 0x47ac3527 at 16818024. So the copy beat the hacker to the first exploit tx by 17 blocks and to the DAI market entirely. It captured $0 for the copier: the DAI sat in the copy until the copier itself called withdraw() (0x3ccfd60b) in block 16818823 (tx 0xdae809e4, 11:38:11Z), which sent all 8,877,507.35 DAI to the hard-coded 0xb66cd966... (hacker's cash-out wallet; same wallet received the hacker's own loot from contract 0x036cec1a). Calls to the copy's withdraw/entry points by other addresses all reverted. Caveats: the copier's claim to be an MEV bot rests on its on-chain message (tx 0x44b559c8..., block 16818973); on-chain it is a fresh single-purpose EOA (nonce 0 at the copy, funded 4.22 ETH on 2023-02-12, no prior MEV history). Whether it saw the hacker's deploy tx in the mempool or only after block 16817993 (12 s earlier) is unknowable: in-block evidence only. It is not a calldata replay of a pending attacker call tx; it is a copy of the attacker's deployment plus an adapted call.
era: 2022-23 post-Merge, MEV-boost (Flashbots relay bids available; no mempool archive: in-block evidence only)
protocol_loss_note: ~$197M total (PeckShield/Euler, from research/candidates, not re-verified); the DAI market part drained by the copier's call = 8,877,507.35 DAI (~$8.88M), which ended at the hacker's wallet

replay_evidence.copied_tx: hacker's CREATE tx 0x50dc9c91... (block 16817993 idx 35), NOT an attacker call tx
replay_evidence.creation_calldata_diff: 17,115 bytes each; 80 differing bytes = 4 x 20-byte address: 0xb2698c2d99ad2c302a95a8db26b08d17a77cedd4 -> 0x5f259d0b76665c337c6104145894f4d1d2758b8c at byte offsets 353, 1454, 7355, 15144; 0xb66cd966670d962c227b3eaba30a872dbfb995db remains in both
replay_evidence.runtime_code: copy #1 and copy #2 runtime code 33,334 bytes each
replay_evidence.call_tree: copy#1 0xc310a0af: DAI decimals x2, DAI balanceOf, Aave LendingPool.flashLoan (0xab9c4b5d, 30M DAI) -> callback 0x920f5c84 into the copy -> Euler (0x27182842) ops -> 38,904,507.35 DAI to the copy -> repay 30,027,000 DAI. Hacker's 0x47ac3527 (WETH variant, entry 0xa91864d4) has the same skeleton with WETH: decimals x2, balanceOf, flashLoan(0xab9c4b5d), callback 0x920f5c84, repay. Entry point 0x863df8af (DAI) exists in the hacker's identical bytecode but the hacker never called it.
replay_evidence.ownership_inference: calls to copy #1/#2 by other EOAs (0x5fb303dc x2, 0xf472e73c, 0x8cbcfa0d x3) all reverted - consistent with an owner check on the swapped constant (not proven; contract logic not otherwise analysed)
replay_evidence.why_funds_went_to_hacker: withdraw() 0x3ccfd60b on the copy calls 0xb66cd966 with ETH and transfers its DAI balance to 0xb66cd966 (trace of 0xdae809e4); 0xb66cd966 is baked in the creation code in both versions. The copier's own withdraw call (block 16818823) executed it ~2h47m after the exploit.

bots.notes: Copier EOA: nonce 0 at the first deploy, received 4.2207 ETH from 0xbcaa6ce6 on 2023-02-12 (that wallet got 2.89 ETH from 0x4e5b2e1d on 2023-02-03; CertiK reports a link to a deflationary-token exploit and Tornado - not verified here). Published its message on-chain at block 16818973 (tx 0x44b559c8, self-transfer): 'I am the owner of a MEV bot that has accidentally frontrun the first tx of the hacker. It tried to frontrun the second tx but failed and only the contract has been created. I tried to return the money but the contract can only send to an address already in bytecode. Unfotunately it sent the money to the hacker's address.'

auction.runner_up_note: 3 later-arriving Flashbots-builder bids were higher (0.09428 @-897ms, 0.09434 @-536ms, 0.09693 @-228ms) but the block received at -1014 ms (0.09425 ETH) was delivered; contents of losing bids unknowable.
auction.ordering_inference: Bot tx idx 0 by priority fee alone: 37.9 gwei tip (effective 56.82 gwei) vs 17.5 gwei for idx 1; no coinbase transfer, so ordering = public gas-price auction (PGA), not a bundle. Hacker's deploy tx in 16817993 paid a 3 gwei tip. Mempool first-seen: none (archive starts 2023-08-07).

evidence_limits: in-block evidence only: no mempool archive for 2023-03-13; unknown whether the copier saw the hacker's CREATE in the mempool or after block 16817993; bundle/PGA status of other txs unverified; losing-bid contents unknowable.
headline_text: A fresh EOA copied the Euler attacker's exploit contract one block after its deploy, swapping only the owner address, and ran its DAI-market entry point at block 16817996 position 0: 8,877,507 DAI out of Euler. Funds went to the attacker's hard-coded wallet; the copier captured nothing.

harmonized.verdict_reason: The copier deployed a bytecode copy (4x20 bytes differ) one block after the attacker's deploy and ran the DAI-market entry point 17 blocks before the hacker's first call; it captured nothing (proceeds went to the hard-coded attacker wallet).
harmonized.headline_note: The copier may be the attacker’s own second account: it was a fresh single-purpose EOA, kept the attacker’s cash-out wallet and captured nothing. Its own on-chain message is the only claim that it was a bot.
